name: t13.second_dataset.analysis
notes: searched 2026-11-11 for a second public vehicle crash-test or crash-pulse set; the candidates found were: the Bridge of Knowledge dataset of vehicle centre-of-gravity accelerations from EN 1317 TB32 impacts (page blocked by an access check, not opened), the Fraunhofer crash-box dataset (component tests, not vehicle pulses, not opened), and NHTSA event-data-recorder report PDFs (reports, not signals). No dataset was opened, so the sensor-requirement and mis-triage analyses were not repeated on a second source

name: sh.holm.hs1.verdict
notes: The impact-side rule keeps side accuracy at or above 0.90 in every sensor variant of the simulated logs.

name: sh.holm.hs2.verdict
notes: The 2 g trigger gives crash recall of at least 0.90 and a non-crash false-alarm rate of at most 0.10 in every sensor variant.

name: sh.holm.hs3.verdict
notes: On link logs calibrated from the four edge runs, UA-SCT delivers at least as often as fixed-3 minus 0.02, within the duty allowance.

name: sh.holm.hs4.verdict
notes: The median trigger-to-ACK latency of first-try deliveries is at least 500 ms (a sub-500 ms statement fails for this window, alert and ACK).

name: sh.holm.hs5.verdict
notes: No attack of the repository's suite and the simulated scenarios is accepted, and the reference verifier persists its counter.

name: sh.holm.hs6.verdict
notes: SW-420 confirmation lowers the non-crash false-alarm rate by at least 0.02 and loses at most 0.02 of the crash recall.

name: sh.holm.family_size
notes: Holm correction over this family, alpha 0.05

name: ar.holm.hr1a.verdict
notes: After a car reboot GTF accepts at least 99% of valid alerts (clock drift up to 5 s, GPS loss up to 40%).

name: ar.holm.hr1b.verdict
notes: GTF replay acceptance is zero outside the window and at most 1% inside it, at the held-out burst loads.

name: ar.holm.hr1c.verdict
notes: GTF cuts flash writes per year at least 10 times against persisting every alert counter.

name: ar.holm.hr2a.verdict
notes: A frame of at most 40 bytes with a 7 or 8 byte tag raises burst delivery by 5 points over the 97-byte frame.

name: ar.holm.hr2b.verdict
notes: The 97-byte frame with an 8-byte tag is dominated, in forgery effort, time on air and delivery, by a frame with a tag of at least 8 bytes.

name: ar.holm.hr3.verdict
notes: A provisional flash from the early-exit rule reaches the base at least 0.8 s earlier, with under 20% retractions, under 40% extra airtime and no delivery loss.

name: ar.holm.hr4.verdict
notes: With per-vehicle ACK keys a forged ACK from a compromised node stops only that node, at one extra KDF per new id and no extra bytes.

name: ar.holm.family_size
notes: Holm correction over this family, alpha 0.05
